title: Loss of force induced by high extracellular [K+] in rat muscle: effect of temperature, lactic acid and beta2-agonist
authors: Pedersen TH, Clausen T, Nielsen OB
population: Isolated rat soleus and extensor digitorum longus muscles
funder: The study was supported by grants from the Danish Medical Research Council (no. 22-01-0189), the Danish Biomembrane Research Centre, Aarhus Universitets Forskningsfond and The Carlsberg Foundation.
result: In isolated rat soleus muscle exposed to 11 mM extracellular K+, tetanic force was 16 ± 4% of control at 30 °C; raising the temperature to 35 °C gave 35 ± 5%, adding 10 mM L-lactic acid 52 ± 3%, and adding 10 µM salbutamol restored force to 87 ± 2%. Together, lactic acid and salbutamol raised the IC50 for extracellular K+ from 10.7 to 13.5 mM. Force recovery produced by warming was suppressed by ouabain, and warming raised ouabain-suppressible 86Rb+ uptake by 93%, lowered intracellular Na+ by 5 mM and hyperpolarised the membrane by 5 mV, so recovery in this preparation depends on Na+-K+ pump activity. The authors ascribe the added effect of salbutamol to a higher affinity of the pump for intracellular Na+.
